standard.title: Differences between text types
standard.description: identify some differences between imaginative and informative texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have been read imaginative and informative texts. They have not yet been explicitly asked to name and compare the differences between these two broad text types as categories.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify and describe differences between imaginative and informative texts — including purpose, content and image use — and can select texts for information purposes.

nodes.label: Some texts are stories, some give information
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify whether a text is imaginative (a story) or informative (giving facts) and say how they know.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one imaginative and one informative text and say one way they are different.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish between imaginative and informative texts; discuss what is 'real' and what is imagined; identify informative texts for information purposes.
wider: Sort a collection of texts into imaginative and informative categories and explain the reasoning for each sort
Find examples where the boundary between imaginative and informative is blurred — for example, narrative non-fiction — and discuss
nodes.hinge_reason: Without the imaginative/informative distinction, students cannot compare how images function differently across text types in Node 2 — the image comparison depends on the category distinction being secure.

response_modes.reason: Students may use a surface feature (pictures = stories) to classify — the misconception is that visual richness signals imaginative purpose. Multiple examples, including illustrated informative texts and wordless stories, help build a more robust criterion.

success_criteria: Student can identify an imaginative text and an informative text from a selection.
Student can say at least one reason for the classification.

nodes.label: Images differ between text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare how images are used differently in imaginative and informative texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one difference in how images are used in an imaginative text and an informative text.
nodes.typical_width: Compare images in imaginative and informative texts — noting that imaginative texts often use illustrations to evoke emotion or narrative while informative texts use images to show, label or explain real content.
wider: Compare the same topic presented in an imaginative and an informative text — examining how images serve different purposes in each
Investigate First Nations Australian texts that serve both imaginative and informative purposes and discuss how images function in them
Discuss how digital informative texts (websites, simple apps) use images differently from print informative texts
success_criteria: Student can describe how images are used differently in an imaginative and an informative text.
Student can give a reason why images in informative texts look different from illustrations in stories.
